title: Pinch-to-resize & virtualized-table fallthroughs for cross-browser console
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Deliver a resilient interaction pattern for small-screen and mixed-input devices across the Redwood Console: enable pinch-to-resize split panels and card containers, improve virtualized table stability, and add deterministic fallbacks for browsers/devices that trigger rendering jitter or memory pressure. The goal is parity of interaction and visual stability across Chrome/Firefox/Safari (desktop + iOS) and Chromium-based mobile browsers while keeping keyboard and screen-reader accessibility intact. This ticket covers finalizing the prototype, capturing cross-browser test results, documenting engineering handoff, and gating acceptance on performance and accessibility metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Pinch-to-resize: two-finger pinch on touch devices should resize left/right split panels and chart height with a fluid animation and no layout flashing on iOS Safari and Chrome for Android
Keyboard parity: resize actions accessible via keyboard (Alt/Ctrl + Arrow) with ARIA announce of new sizes

Virtualized table stability: continuous scrolling without row jump artifacts across tested browsers; when platform causes instability (Safari memory spikes or older Android webview), UI falls back to paginated windowing with prefetch and the switch is seamless
Chart fallbacks: Canvas charts degrade to SVG+lightweight sparklines on browsers where incremental canvas redraw causes jank; charts keep tooltips and keyboard focus order
Cross-browser visual regressions: no visual regressions in core dashboard, cost-explorer and rollouts pages per Percy snapshots
Performance: 95th-percentile interaction latency for resize and table scroll < 120ms on representative devices used in tests
Accessibility: Manual NVDA/VoiceOver checks for resizing announced correctly and focus is preserved after fallbacks
decisions: Use a hybrid approach: continuous CSS transforms for visual fluidity, but commit final size with layout writes throttled to rAF to minimize reflow on low-end devices

Keep virtualization as default for large datasets; implement deterministic detection of instability (memory usage, long task spikes, or observe scroll jitter heuristics) and switch to paginated mode rather than trying to patch every browser-specific virtualization bug
Prefer feature-detection over user-agent sniffing. Use IntersectionObserver and ResizeObserver where available; provide explicit shims and clear telemetry when fallback is triggered
Charts: prefer canvas for high-density renderers but include SVG fallback layers for Safari where repeated canvas clears produced flicker in prototypes
reviews: 2025-03-06 - PM review (Jules Park): good trade-offs, verify metrics for fallback decision threshold
2025-03-10 - Accessibility review (Samir Rao): recommended ARIA live-region for resize announcements; ensure keyboard triggers are discoverable
2025-03-14 - Engineering review (Priya Singh): requested concrete heuristics for jitter detection and a small API for toggling fallbacks from runtime
2025-03-17 - Design critique (Lena Ortiz): micro-interaction polish suggested — add subtle easing and preserved baseline when snap-resizing to common widths
usability_testing: Prototype tested in moderated session (6 participants): pinch-to-resize was intuitive for 5/6; one participant expected a handle affordance — action: add optional visual handle on hover/focus

Unmoderated cohort (20 sessions across iOS Safari and Chrome Android): 4 sessions triggered fallback due to memory warnings on older Android; transition felt abrupt in 2/4 cases — engineering to add smooth crossfade
Screen reader sessions (3): resize announcements were clear after ARIA live-region implementation; one edge case where focus lost after table fallthrough fixed
cross_browser_matrix: Chrome Desktop (latest): pass — virtualization stable; pinch not applicable
Firefox Desktop (latest): pass with minor redraw threshold tweaks
Safari Desktop (macOS Sonoma): pass with SVG fallback for charts enabled
Safari iOS (17.x): pinch-to-resize works; had layout flashing before rAF commit; fixed in prototype v3
Chrome Android (old webview): virtualization unstable for very large result sets; triggers paginated fallback
Edge Chromium (Windows 10): pass — minor scrollbar overlap fixed via padding tweak
next_steps: Final engineering handoff: attach jitter detection heuristics and observable telemetry events
Design QA pass after engineering prototype (verify easing, handle affordance, focus order)
Add automated Percy snapshots for the main pages under both virtualization and paginated states
Follow-up ticket to add admin toggle for forcing fallbacks in Dedicated/private deployments for debugging
